rulers.name: Flaccitheus
rulers.note: The page's list gives 454-475; its infobox gives 467-475 ('By 467, the Rugii ruled a kingdom based in Lower Austria').

rulers.name: Feletheus
rulers.note: Defeated by Odoacer in 487; executed with his wife in Ravenna in 487. His son Frideric was claimant 487-492/493 (not a ruler of the realm).

correction.text: the Waldviertel and Weinviertel north of the Danube

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 454: the Rugii rebel against the Huns ('In 453') and settle 'in the counties of Waldviertel and Weinviertel', north of the Danube in Lower Austria; the page's reign list starts Flaccitheus in 454. Cliopatria's shape starts in 455 and is used a year early.

14,368 km2 (59 cells), bbox 13.7-16.9 E, 48.3-49.0 N: 40 cells in Lower Austria, 13 in Upper Austria and 6 in Czechia (gazetteer check). The page gives the Waldviertel and Weinviertel, north of the Danube in Lower Austria, and no area; the Upper Austrian and Czech cells are Cliopatria's and are not on the page ('never part of the Roman province of Noricum').
14,526 km2, the same ground. In 476 Feletheus supported Odoacer's Herulian and Scirian mercenaries, who overthrew Romulus Augustus.

14,526 km2 for 480-489, but 'Odoacer subsequently invaded the Kingdom of the Rugii, where he utterly defeated the Rugian troops' in 487, and the page adds no Rugian realm after that (the Rugii joined Theodoric in 489). The shape holds to 487.

region.text: Waldviertel and Weinviertel, Lower Austria north of the Danube

ledger.note: 454: the Rugii settle north of the Danube after Nedao. 'In 453, they successfully rebelled against the Huns along with other Germanic tribes at the Battle of Nedao' and settled 'in the counties of Waldviertel and Weinviertel, which lie north of the Danube'; the Nedao page dates the battle 454 and names the Rugii among the peoples independent by the early 460s; the page's infobox has the kingdom established in 467 under Flaccitheus.

487: Odoacer conquers the Rugian kingdom. 'Odoacer subsequently invaded the Kingdom of the Rugii, where he utterly defeated the Rugian troops'; Feletheus and his wife were 'executed in Ravenna in 487' (the Odoacer page: '487/488 ... against the Rugians in Noricum').

487: the Rugian kingdom ends with Odoacer's victory. The page gives no end date; the infobox: 'the Rugian king Feletheus is defeated by King of Italy Odoacer: 487'. Frideric is claimant to 492/493, and 'Two years later, the Rugii joined the Ostrogothic king Theodoric' (489).

wars.name: Battle of Nedao
wars.outcome: The Rugii, with other Germanic peoples, break Hunnic rule and settle north of the Danube; independent by the early 460s.
wars.note: The Rugiland page dates the battle 453, the Nedao page 454.

wars.name: Odoacer's campaign against the Rugii
wars.outcome: Odoacer defeats the Rugian troops, takes Feletheus to Ravenna and has him executed; the Rugian land is later settled by Lombards.
wars.note: Odoacer page: 'In 487/488, Odoacer led his army to victory against the Rugians in Noricum'.

certainty.note: A kingdom north of the Danube with the river as its south edge; the other frontiers are tribal and unsurveyed.

notes: Cliopatria's Rugiland row runs 455-489 (14,526 km2); the pages give 487 for Odoacer's victory, so the dossier ends 487 and the 480 shape is trimmed. The start is 454 by the Nedao page and the reign list; the Rugiland page also gives 453 (the rebellion) and 467 (the kingdom, infobox), so the year is soft. The page's infobox names the capital as Vindobona (Vienna), but Vindobona lies south of the Danube, outside the Rugian land north of the river and outside every Rugiland shape, so no capital is drawn. [Reviewer eu-06-d: corrected; the infobox does name a capital.] The Lombard settlement of the land is undated on the page; the Lombards row (eu-06) starts 480. The Sciri and Heruli, Odoacer's mercenaries in 476, have no dossier (counterparts_needing_dossiers). Severinus and Noricum Ripense are not on the page; the page says the Rugian land was 'never part of the Roman province of Noricum'. No infobox area on the page. Rugii remnants joining Theodoric in 489 appear in the Ostrogoths dossier (Rugii 'joined the Ostrogoths in their invasion of Italy', Ostrogoths page).
